transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-28 16:00 UTC — Duration: 58m
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE) — Evan Riley (CISO), Priya Malhotra (Head Cloud Eng), Samir Patel (SRE), Olivia Zhang (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick tabletop focused on SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM orchestration, audit log retention, and the BCDR escalation ladder (RTO/RPO specifics). Walkthrough of a simulated region outage and how Redwood fallbacks (model variants, dedicated vs hosted) and private KMS behave.

Topics covered:
- SSO/SAML + RBAC mapping to Redwood Console roles
- KMS integration patterns (bring-your-own keys, HSM-backed rotation)
- Audit logs, retention, and export for auditors
- RTO/RPO expectations and multi-region failover sequence
- SLA escalation chain and oncall handoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call, and we'll kick off — we planned a tabletop — i think priya you were going to outline current rto targets?
[00:22] Priya: yeah um hi, thanks. so currently our app teams are at RTO 2 hours and RPO 15 minutes for core services, but for ai inference pipelines we were hoping to target 30 minutes rto, 5 minute rpo if possible — that's aggressive i know
[00:40] Maya: ok that's helpful, we'll map that to Redwood dedicated failover options. for RTO you want model warm pools, prefix cache recovery, and cross-region kv cache sync — though kv cache is tricky with h s m sorry kv cache like key value cache consistency
[01:05] Samir: can you back up on the kv cache bit? we've seen stale caches cause bad outputs, so we prefer cold start with recovered kv rather than desynced prefixes
[01:20] Liam: totally, and you can choose policies. Redwood can do graceful fallback to a smaller model variant while kv rebuilds, so latency spikes but correctness is preserved. on the k m s side we support BYOK via HSMs — we have a sample runbook for key rotation and midnight key handover
[01:45] Evan: okay evan here — two questions: 1) are audit logs immutable? 2) if keys are BYOK and customer-managed, how do you handle cross-region key availability during failover?
[02:05] Jordan: great q. audit logs are append-only in the control plane and we provide tamper-evident export to your s3. integrity is by signed digests. for BYOK, we have two patterns: replicate keys in your HSM cluster (preferred), or use a regional KMS proxy with strict RBAC and emergency key export policies
[02:35] Olivia: auditors will want chain-of-custody. can you create an export that shows key rotations, who triggered them, and the k m s policy version?
[02:50] Maya: yes, we can provide a rotation timeline and signer metadata. small caveat: some fields are redacted when using third-party HSMs depending on vendor audit constraints
[03:15] Priya: what's the SSO mapping look like? we use Okta with SCIM groups and want least-privilege mapped to Redwood Console roles, with separation for SEs vs devs
[03:30] Liam: we map SCIM groups to Redwood RBAC roles — admin, ops, viewer, model-manager. Okta assertion maps to the role at login, and we support SAML SSO and OIDC. there can be a lag on group sync — we recommend an on-demand sync button for emergencies
[04:00] Samir: about escalation — walk me through a real outage timeline. say primary region 1 goes down at 10:00, what's the sequence?
[04:15] Jordan: first minute: automatic detection via heartbeat, route to canary region. minutes 0–5: automatic routing to DR region using policy 'latency-first' or 'cost-first' depending on tag. minute 5–20: attempts to bring dedicated warm pools up; if keys aren't available the system will try KMS proxy then alert the oncall and progression to manual key import
[04:45] Evan: if manual import is needed who is responsible? our compliance requires a named owner and audit trail
[04:55] Jordan: we propose an escalation chain: Redwood SE oncall -> Redwood infra engineer (named) -> customer cloud engineer (Priya) -> CISO (Evan). each step logs approver and action. we'll include contact windows and SLA targets in the runbook
[05:20] Olivia: worried about SLA credits — what does your SLA cover for cross-region failover time?
[05:30] Maya: our SLA covers uptime for inference endpoints; standard credit policy is based on p95 latency and monthly availability. cross-region failover time is considered incident-dependent; for Dedicated customers we can add explicit failover SLOs in the contract
[05:55] Priya: also need a runbook snippet for legal — a simple sequence: detection, auto-route, key-check, manual-import, failover-confirm, postmortem. with responsibilities and timestamps
[06:15] Jordan: we'll draft that. quick note: some customers require air-gapped key escrow; in those cases Redwood's private deployment supports an HSM plug-in behind your firewall, we provide an automation agent for key rotation but the private key material never leaves your HSM
[06:40] Samir: can we test key rotation during a failover? like a controlled test where we rotate keys and ensure the DR path can decrypt?
[06:52] Maya: yes, that's part of our recommended quarterly drills. we do a staged rotation: replicate rotation in DR HSM, validate signer chain, then fail traffic and verify model decryption — we can script it with our playbook
[07:10] Evan: what about audit log retention for e-discovery? we need 7 years for some data classes
[07:20] Liam: Redwood supports configurable retention up to 10 years for exported logs; long-term archives are stored in your account s3 with immutability flags (WORM) if required
[07:40] Olivia: any gotchas with GDPR/data residency during failover? we are EU-first tenants
[07:50] Jordan: yes, cross-region failover to non-EU regions is opt-in. we support region pinning and also automatic anonymization of payload before failover if policy set. that means some requests may be redacted to avoid residency breaches
[08:10] Priya: regression testing — will Redwood help with benchmark tests for latency during failover? we want numbers under 300ms for p50 for our prioritized routes
[08:22] Maya: we can run a benchmark harness and provide per-route p50/p95 during drills; note model variant changes can affect tokenization speed so we typically recommend canary runs with your prompt set
[08:40] Samir: ok let's talk contacts and escalation timings — what is Redwood's target response time for SE oncall?
[08:50] Jordan: SE oncall initial ack within 15 minutes, engineer assignment within 1 hour for P1. we can tighten those windows in enterprise contracts
[09:05] Evan: and post-incident postmortem cadence? we need blameless PM within 72 hours and final report with root cause in 10 business days
[09:20] Jordan: that's fine, we'll adapt to your cadence
[09:30] Maya: one more technical note — for KV cache sync we recommend asynchronous replication with tombstone markers to avoid replay hazards; there are tradeoffs between strict consistency and RTO. you told us you'd prefer correctness over latency?
[09:45] Priya: yes correctness first for our case, latency can be tolerated during failover windows
[09:52] Liam: ok then we'll propose a slow rebuild with fallback variants. we'll include a config sample: rebuild window 30–90 minutes, fallback model variant for 0–30 minutes
[10:10] Jordan: recap & next steps — we'll send the KMS/HSM runbook, provide the RBAC mapping guide for Okta, draft the incident escalation ladder with named roles, and propose dates for a failover drill
[10:30] Evan: good. also please include pricing delta for dedicated warm pools and cross-region replication — procurement will need that in the follow-up
[10:40] Jordan: noted. any other questions?
[10:48] Olivia: can you also include a sample export of audit logs with redaction examples? auditors like to see it
[10:55] Maya: yes we'll include that as CSV and sample signed digest
[11:05] Priya: perfect, thanks everyone. let's book the drill for mid april
[11:12] Jordan: thanks all. bye

End of meeting.
